title: Adaptive Soft Rolling KV Freeze with Entropy-Guided Recovery: Sublinear Memory Growth for Efficient LLM Inference
one_line_claim: Training-free KV cache compression via reversible soft-freezing with entropy-guided recovery achieves 55-67% compression while maintaining generation quality.
method_summary: ASR-KF-EGR temporarily freezes low-importance KV pairs (identified via attention entropy scores within a sliding window) to CPU storage rather than permanently evicting them, using a sublinear freeze schedule d_j = floor(sqrt(c_j)/k) where c_j counts prior low-importance detections, enabling dynamic restoration when context requirements shift.

key_findings.finding: Achieves 55-67% KV cache compression on LLaMA-3 8B while maintaining generation quality.
key_findings.quote: Preliminary experiments on LLaMA-3 8B demonstrate that ASR-KF-EGR achieves 55-67% compression ratios while maintaining generation quality and passing retrieval benchmarks

key_findings.finding: On a 500-token generation stress test, reduces active KV cache size by 66.93% while keeping tokens recoverable in off-GPU storage.
key_findings.quote: As shown in Table 1, ASR-KF-EGR reduces active KV cache size by 66.93% while maintaining all tokens in recoverable storage.

key_findings.finding: Successfully passes needle-in-haystack retrieval tasks, preserving ability to recover specific information from compressed context.
key_findings.quote: ASR-KF-EGR successfully retrieves the embedded passkey (Table 2), demonstrating that the freezing mechanism does not permanently lose critical information.

key_findings.finding: Exhibits sublinear memory growth versus linear growth of standard KV caching as sequence length increases.
key_findings.quote: While the baseline grows linearly, ASR-KF-EGR exhibits sublinear growth with characteristic oscillations as tokens cycle through freeze and unfreeze states.

relation_to_herald.shared: Both monitor per-token signals during autoregressive generation to guide runtime intervention Both use zero-cost features extracted from attention computations as decision signals Both target KV-cache dynamics in LLM inference without requiring model fine-tuning Both aim to preserve generation quality while addressing KV-cache resource constraints Both operate within a time-series framework of token-by-token decisions
differs_on: Intervention target: ASR-KF-EGR modulates compression aggressiveness to maintain quality; HERALD predicts looping/non-termination onset to enable external intervention before catastrophic failure
Signal type: ASR-KF-EGR uses attention interaction entropy scores (Eq. 2: s_j as mean attention magnitude); HERALD uses per-token logit probability distributions as time-series features
Scope: ASR-KF-EGR is a self-modulating compressor; HERALD is a separate monitor/alarm that flags hazard onset without controlling the compression system
